lesson.title: How a hash table stores keys
lesson.goal: See keys hashed into buckets with key mod capacity, collisions resolved by chaining or probing, and the table resized when it fills.

say: A hash table turns each key into a bucket number with key mod capacity. Twelve mod four is zero, and seven mod four is three.
Nine mod four is one, an empty bucket. Thirteen also lands in bucket one, so it joins the chain there.
Four keys now fill four buckets, so the table doubles to eight. Every key is hashed again with mod eight.
With open addressing each bucket holds just one key. Three mod two is one, a taken bucket, so three is turned away and probes bucket zero.
Both buckets are full now. The table grows to four buckets and rehashes every key.
